title: 16.9 Is Still 16! Signum and [x] Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Someone who is 16.9 years old says they are 16, not 17: age always rounds down. But what is -2.1 rounded down: -2 or -3? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we meet two special functions: the signum function and the greatest integer function.

You will watch x slide along a live graph while the signum function keeps only the sign, see why NCERT also writes it as |x|/x, and find [x] by listing the integers to the left of x. Then x runs and the greatest integer function draws itself as a staircase, filled dot by filled dot. Two pause-and-think questions, the rule [x] = n exactly when n <= x < n + 1, a worked example (solve 2[x] - 1 = 5), the exam trap with negative numbers, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Why 16.9 is still 16
0:30 Signum: keep only the sign (live graph)
1:05 Signum written with the modulus
1:31 The greatest integer function [x]
1:59 Chopping vs rounding down: -2.1
2:34 Live: the staircase graph
3:37 Worked example: 2[x] - 1 = 5
4:13 Exam trap: [-3.7]
4:27 Where it is asked
4:35 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:15 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 22): Graphs of Standard Functions. One sheet of graph paper, six different shapes: can you name each one from its graph?
